blocks.heading: WHAT ARE CLOUDWATCH AND BILLING?
blocks.board_text:
CloudWatch = AWS's monitoring system.
Every AWS service sends data to it automatically.
You use that data to set alarms — get notified when something is wrong.

AWS Billing = what you're spending and what's driving it.
Cost Explorer: see spending by service, by day, by region.
Budgets: set a monthly limit, get alerted before you exceed it.

Together:
CloudWatch tells you when your system is broken.
Billing tells you when your spending is broken.
blocks.ren_voice: Week close panna rendu final services. CloudWatch, AWS-oda monitoring system. Every AWS service — EC2, S3, RDS, everything — automatically CloudWatch-ku metrics anuppuchu. Metrics numbers: CPU percentage, error rate, requests per second, database connection count. Andha metrics-la mela alarms set pannuvaanga. Alarm solluchu: idha number, idha threshold-a cross pannaa, idha neram, notify pannu. AWS Billing cost layer. Cost Explorer, namba spend pannatha service-by-service, day-by-day show pannum. AWS Budgets, monthly spending limit set panna allow pannum, 80%, 100%, or namba choose panna threshold-la alert anuppuchu. CloudWatch, system broken-nu solluchu. Billing, spending broken-nu solluchu. Rendu-um watch panna vendiyathu.

check_question.question: What is the difference between a CloudWatch metric and a CloudWatch alarm?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly right — metric, raw number continuously collect aaguchu (CPU at 73%, 5 errors per minute). Alarm, andha metric-la mela set panna rule (CPU 5 minutes 90%-ku mela irundha, notification anuppu). Metrics data, alarms andha data pathi decisions.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Ippadi yosinga: metric number — measured and stored continuously, just raw value. Alarm action layer — metric-la mela rule define pannuvaanga, threshold cross aanappo alarm fire aaguchu, notify pannum. Metric = enna measured aaguchu. Alarm = adhai vachhu enna pannaradhu.

blocks.heading: WHY MONITORING AND BILLING CONTROLS ARE NOT OPTIONAL
blocks.board_text:
Without CloudWatch alarms:
• Your server crashes at 2am
• You find out at 9am when the support tickets arrive
• Users experienced 7 hours of downtime

Without billing controls:
• A test environment runs unmonitored for 6 weeks
• Wrong instance size: ₹4.2 lakhs
• A ₹500/month budget alert would have caught it in week 1

Both are preventable. Both happen constantly. Both kill startups — one through user trust, one through cash burn.
blocks.ren_voice: Monitoring alarms illaadhappo, users-kitta irundhu problem therinjukkuvaanga, system-kitta irundhu illai. 2am-la oru server memory run out aaguchu. Users errors paakuvaanga. Team thoongudhu. Kaalailayae, support tickets 7 hours munnaadi enna nadhanchunu solluvaanga. Andha gap — problem start aana time, team therinjukkara time — completely preventable. Oru CloudWatch alarm on memory utilization irundha, minutes-la notify aagirukum. Billing controls illaadhappo, month-end surprises. Real case: oru team new feature evaluate panna test environment deploy panna. Evaluation wrap up aanaa, nobody shut down pannala. Six weeks run aanaa, wrong instance size. Invoice ₹4.2 lakhs. ₹10,000 per month budget alert irundha, week one-la fire aagirukum. Rendu-um 5 minutes setup-la preventable.

check_question.question: Why is 'we'll check the dashboard occasionally' not a reliable monitoring strategy?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly — dashboards-a yaaravadhu paakka vendiyathu. Alarms proactive — avanga namba-ku find pannum. 3am-la dashboard paakkaara yarum illaadhappo, problem catch aagaadhu, morning-la theriyum. Alarms immediately notify pannum, problem evadha nadhanthaalum, yarum paakkadhappo kooda.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: 3am-la, weekend-la, holiday-la dashboard-a yaaru paakkuvaanga — yarum illai. Problems working hours-la schedule panna povaadhu. Alarms difference — yaravadhu paakka wait pannaadhaa, threshold cross aana moment reach out pannum. Dashboards context-ku, alarms action-ku.

blocks.heading: HOW CLOUDWATCH AND BILLING WORK
blocks.board_text:
CloudWatch — how to set an alarm:
1. Choose a metric (EC2 CPU utilization, S3 request count, RDS connections)
2. Set the threshold (e.g. CPU > 90%)
3. Set the evaluation period (e.g. for 5 consecutive minutes)
4. Set the action (send email, send SMS, trigger auto-scaling)

AWS Budgets — how to set a budget:
1. Choose budget type: Cost Budget
2. Set the amount: your expected monthly spend
3. Set alert thresholds: 80% and 100% of budget
4. Set notification: email to the team

Both take under 5 minutes. Both should exist before anything goes live.
blocks.ren_voice: CloudWatch alarm setup: metric choose pannuvaanga — EC2 CPU utilization-nu. Threshold set pannuvaanga: CPU 90%-ku mela irundha trigger. Evaluation period set pannuvaanga: 5 consecutive minutes-ku mela 90%-la irundha mattum trigger — momentary spikes-ku false alarms prevent. Action configure pannuvaanga: email anuppu, SMS anuppu, or auto-scaling trigger panni automatically more servers launch. Alarm active, watching. AWS Budgets: Cost Budget choose pannu, monthly amount set pannu — deployed resources-ku expected spend — 80% and 100% alert thresholds. Notification email add pannu. Budget exceed panna track-la irundha, email kidaikkum. Adhu mattum. Rendu-um 5 minutes than setup. Rendu-um anything goes live-ku munnaadi irukkanum. No exceptions.

check_question.question: Why do you set a CloudWatch alarm to trigger after 5 consecutive minutes above a threshold, rather than triggering immediately on the first spike?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Right — single spike momentary and harmless-a irukkalam. Traffic burst-la 10 seconds-ku 95% CPU spike, necessarily problem illai. 5 minutes sustained high CPU, very likely real problem. Evaluation period noise filter — normal fluctuations-la alarms fire panna prevent, genuinely attention venum situations-ku reserve panna.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Systems actually eppadi behave pannum-nu yosinga. CPU usage constantly spike and drop — adhu normal. Oru moment-la 90%-ku mela, necessarily problem illai. Five consecutive minutes-la 90%-ku mela, very likely real problem. Evaluation period noise filter — normal fluctuations-la alarm fire panna prevent panna, genuinely action venum situations-ku alert reserve panna.

blocks.heading: WHAT THIS LOOKS LIKE IN THE AWS CONSOLE
blocks.board_text:
CloudWatch console:
→ Services → Management & Governance → CloudWatch
→ 'Dashboards' → Create Dashboard → add widgets: EC2 CPU, S3 requests, RDS connections
→ 'Alarms' → Create Alarm → select metric → set threshold → set notification
→ Alarm list shows: metric, threshold, current state (OK / ALARM / INSUFFICIENT_DATA)

AWS Budgets:
→ Services → Billing → Budgets → Create Budget
→ Monthly cost budget → set amount → alert thresholds → notification email
→ Budget list shows: budget amount, current spend, forecast for the month
blocks.ren_voice: CloudWatch console: Services → Management and Governance → CloudWatch. Left-la Dashboards and Alarms. Create Dashboard click pannaa, widgets add pannuvaanga — EC2 CPU utilization, S3 request count, RDS connections — andha numbers real time-la update aaguchu, live view. Alarms click pannaa, active alarms ellam. Oru alarm, watch panna metric, threshold, current state show pannum: OK means normal range-la, ALARM means threshold crossed, alert fired, INSUFFICIENT_DATA means not enough data collected. Alarm create: Create Alarm click, searchable list-la metric pick, threshold and evaluation period set, notification configure. AWS Budgets: Services → Billing → Budgets. Budgets-oda amount, current spend, month-end forecast. Create Budget click panni new one setup pannuvaanga.

check_question.question: In the CloudWatch Alarms list, you see an alarm in ALARM state. What does that tell you, and what is your immediate next step?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Right — ALARM state, threshold cross aanaa, evaluation period sustained-nu. Yedhaavadhu genuinely wrong. Next step: alarm click pannaa, which metric trigger aannu, current value enna-nu paakka, apparam andha metric generate panna resource investigate panna — EC2 instance, RDS database, whatever.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: ALARM state threshold cross aanaa, evaluation period sustained-nu — false alarm illai, real signal. Next step investigate. Alarm click pannu, which metric trigger aannu, current value enna-nu paaru, apparam andha resource — EC2 instance, RDS database, metric generate panna edhuvaavathu — enna nadhakutu-nu paaru.

blocks.heading: YOUR TURN — WHAT WOULD YOU DO?
blocks.board_text:
Scenario:
It is 11pm. A CloudWatch alarm fires — your EC2 instance's CPU utilization has been at 95% for the last 10 minutes.

What are the first two things you check in the CloudWatch console to diagnose what is happening?
blocks.ren_voice: Raathiri 11 manikku. Alarm fire aaguchu. EC2 instance 10 minutes-ku 95% CPU-la irukkum. AWS console open pannuveenga. CloudWatch-la enna paakkaradhu-nu yosinga — first enna information venum, then enna?

check_question.question: Walk me through your first two diagnostic steps in CloudWatch.
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Good — first, CPU metric graph paaru, timeline-a: evadha spike aannu, still climbing-aa leveling off-aa, innaikku earlier pattern irundhanaa. Second, andha instance or application-ku CloudWatch Logs check pannu, CPU spike-oda correlate panna application errors or unusual activity paaru. Timeline and logs, root cause-ku fastest paths.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Sequence-a solren. First, CPU metric graph — current value mattum illai, timeline. CPU climbing evadha start aannu? Still going up-aa? Suddenly-aa gradually-aa? Problem evadha start aannu-nu solluchu. Second, andha instance or application-ku CloudWatch Logs check — errors, unusual request patterns, or CPU spike same time-la enna nadhanchunu. Timeline first, logs second.

blocks.heading: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU SKIP BILLING ALERTS
blocks.board_text:
A real case:
A team deployed a test environment to evaluate a new feature.
No billing alert set. The evaluation ended. Nobody shut it down.

What happened:
• Test environment ran unmonitored for 6 weeks
• EC2 instance: wrong size for the workload — running at 10% utilization
• EBS volumes attached but unused
• NAT Gateway running for 6 weeks, zero traffic
• Month-end invoice: ₹4.2 lakhs
• A ₹10,000/month budget alert would have fired in week 1
blocks.ren_voice: Ithu expect panna vida often happen aaguchu. Oru team new feature test panna test environment spin up pannuvaanga — EC2, RDS, EBS, NAT Gateway. Evaluation pannivaanga. Feature shelved. Everybody next thing-ku move on. Nobody explicitly test environment shut down pannala, yen-naa habit illai. Six weeks piragu, monthly invoice varuchu. ₹4.2 lakhs. Everybody confused. Trace pannuvaanga — test environment entire time run aanaa. EC2 instance wrong size, 10% utilization-la run aanaa. EBS volumes attached, charge aanaa. NAT Gateway exactly zero bytes traffic process pannuchu, aaana per hour bill aanaa. ₹10,000 per month budget alert week one-la fire aagirukum. Idle environment find panna investigate panna, shut down panna. Total cost ₹15,000-ku kella irukkum. Aaana: ₹4.2 lakhs.

check_question.question: Beyond a billing alert, what habit would have prevented this scenario entirely?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Right — every test resource-ku expiry date or owner tag. Test environment-ku cleanup eppadu panna, yaar ownerpaarunga-nu tag irundha, weekly expired or untagged resources audit panna process irundha, idle environments 6 weeks survive aagaadhu. Billing alerts nadhanthaappo catch pannum; habit nadhakkaadhapadiyae prevent pannum.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Ithai cause pannatha yosinga: nobody test environments cleanup panna habit illai. Billing alert week one-la catch pannirukkum, aaana underlying problem, test resources cleanup plan illaamal create pannaacha. Build panna habit: every test resource-ku owner and expiry date tag pannu, weekly 'test'-nu match panna or expiry pass panna resources cleanup review pannunga. Prevention, detection-ai vida nalla.

blocks.heading: QUICK CHALLENGE
blocks.board_text:
Your company's production app just went down.
You open CloudWatch.

You see these metrics all showing abnormal values at the same time:
• EC2 CPU: 12% (very low)
• ALB Request Count: dropped to zero
• RDS CPU: 98% (very high)

Based on these three metrics, what is most likely the cause?
blocks.ren_voice: Production app just went down. CloudWatch-la moonu metrics same time-la abnormal values show pannuvaanga. EC2 CPU 12% — much lower than normal. ALB request count zero-ku drop — servers-ku traffic reach panna illai. RDS CPU 98% — database hammered. Idha combination enna solluchu, problem engey irukku?

check_question.question: What is the most likely cause, based on the pattern of these three metrics?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Correct — database likely culprit. RDS 98% CPU, overloaded and slow. ALB requests zero-ku drop aaguchu, yen-naa database-a wait panna app requests fail or timeout aaguchu. EC2 CPU low, yen-naa servers idle — database-a wait pannikittu, processing panna illai. Pattern, database problem-ku point pannum, server problem illai.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Pattern serndhu paarunga. EC2 CPU low — servers work panna illai. Aana ALB traffic zero-ku drop — users app-ku reach panna illai. RDS 98% — database maxed out. Database overwhelmed-na, EC2-kitta irundhu queries timeout or fail aaguchu. App errors return pannum. Load balancer unhealthy targets-a paakuchu, traffic route pannaadhaa. Low EC2 CPU + high RDS CPU + zero traffic = database problem, servers illai.

blocks.heading: HOW FLIPKART MONITORS DURING BIG BILLION DAYS
blocks.board_text:
Flipkart — Big Billion Days sale, one of India's largest traffic events:

• Engineering team watches CloudWatch dashboards live on a big screen throughout the event
• Alarms set at 60%, 80%, 95% of every capacity threshold — not just 100%
• Billing alerts at 50% and 80% of expected daily cost
• If a metric crosses 80%, investigation starts before 100% is reached
• Incident response time target: under 3 minutes from alarm to first response
• Result: the team sees problems before customers do, every time
blocks.ren_voice: Flipkart-oda Big Billion Days, Indian technology-la highest-stakes traffic events-la oru. Millions concurrent users, flash sales, live countdowns — 5 minutes outage peak hours-la significant revenue and trust loss. Avanga engineering team eppadi approach pannaanga-nu paarkalam. CloudWatch dashboards war room-la big screen-la sale-a throughout run aaguchu. Alarms normal-a vida more aggressively set — 100% capacity-ku mattum illai, 60%, 80%, 95%-la kooda. Metric 80% hit aanappo, team already investigate panna, decisions panna start aaguchu. Goal: user impact cause panna threshold reach pannaadhappu munnaadi act pannardhu, piragu illai. Billing alerts expected daily spend-oda 50% and 80%-la — traffic-driven costs expected levels-ku mela surge aanaa, immediately team-ku theriyum. Incident response target: alarm fire aanaa first human response 3 minutes-ku kella. Adhu-taan scale-la monitoring matter aanappo eppadi irukkunu.

lesson_summary.board_text:
What you must know after Day 5:

• CloudWatch collects metrics from all AWS services automatically — you set alarms on top
• Alarms = proactive notification. Dashboards = visibility. Both are needed.
• Set billing alerts before spending anything — not after the invoice arrives
• Minimum before going live: CPU alarm, error rate alarm, monthly budget alert at 80%
• Never wait for users to tell you something is broken — that is what monitoring is for
lesson_summary.ren_voice: Day 5 aavudhu. CloudWatch namba system watch pannum — every metric, every service, continuously. Alarms threshold cross aanappo reach out pannum, 3am-la, Sunday-la, eppo-va. Billing alerts month-end surprises-la irundhu protect pannum. Anything goes live-ku munnaadi minimum: every EC2 instance-ku CPU alarm, API-ku error rate alarm, monthly budget-oda 80%-la alert. First server start aagathukku munnaadi ithai setup pannu. Monitoring later add panna vishayam illai. Ithu infrastructure. Andha week aavudhu — cloud, identity, networking, compute and storage, monitoring cover pannaacha. Ithu foundation. Work starts from here.
